output.contract_title: Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) with Enterprise Partner 025 LLC

clauses.clause_text: Customer shall pay all undisputed invoice amounts within thirty (30) days of invoice date.
Vendor shall notify Customer in writing within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of any confirmed Data Breach.
Each party's maximum aggregate liability shall be strictly limited to the total fees paid under this Agreement in the preceding twelve (12) months.
Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon providing thirty (30) days prior written notice.
This Agreement renews on an annual basis unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 30 days prior.

extraction_notes: Document extracted once for downstream policy comparison

mandatory_requirements.description: Vendor must notify customer of any security breach within 48 hours of discovery.
Data must be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.3 and at rest using AES-256.

ambiguities_in_policy: The term "discovery" is not defined; it may be interpreted differently across vendors.
No specification of time zone for the 48‑hour notification window.
No guidance on key management practices for AES‑256 encryption at rest.

mappings.notes: Vendor notifies within 24 hours, which meets the 48‑hour notification requirement.
No extracted clause specifies encryption in transit (TLS 1.3) or at rest (AES‑256).

deviations.supporting_evidence: Mapping notes indicate no extracted clause specifies encryption in transit (TLS 1.3) or at rest (AES-256). Policy requires data to be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.3 and at rest using AES-256.
deviations.recommended_remediation: Add a dedicated data protection clause that explicitly mandates encryption of all data in transit using TLS 1.3 and encryption at rest using AES-256. Include compliance verification steps (e.g., periodic security audits, certification of encryption mechanisms) and penalties for non‑compliance.

risk_findings.ambiguity_description: The term "undisputed invoice amounts" is not defined, leaving ambiguity around what constitutes a dispute and how disputes are resolved. No interest or penalty for late payment is specified, favoring the vendor.

"Becoming aware of any confirmed Data Breach" is undefined; it is unclear when a breach is considered "confirmed" and what triggers the awareness. This creates uncertainty around the notification timeline.

Limiting aggregate liability to the total fees paid in the preceding twelve months may be insufficient to cover potential damages, especially for data breach or intellectual property losses. The cap is symmetric but may disproportionately expose the customer to higher risk.

Termination for convenience is allowed by either party with 30 days' notice, but the clause does not address post‑termination obligations such as data return, transition services, or outstanding fees, creating operational uncertainty.

The renewal clause lacks details on renewal terms, such as price adjustments, service level changes, or notice mechanisms beyond the 30‑day non‑renewal period, leading to potential commercial exposure at renewal.
